content_of_post_to_answer: Can knowledge enter a mind whose door is closed?
answer: A closed mind is rarely a lack of information; it is often a protective mechanism. People reject knowledge not because they cannot understand it, but because accepting it may threaten an identity, belief, or comfort they are attached to. This is why facts alone do not always create learning. A mind opens when curiosity becomes stronger than the need to be right. Knowledge does not enter through force; it enters through willingness.
